messages.text: The build has reached runtime and MCP. Compilation is still clean; I’m waiting for nextest to begin reporting test results.
The same build is still running without errors. Tests haven’t started, and the source tree remains unchanged.

Compilation succeeded, and nextest is running all 458 selected tests. The first 120 have passed with no failures. That total covers the 136 core schema/migration tests, focused 163, and 159 Rust usages tests.

457 of 458 tests have passed, including the three queue regressions, route-precedence golden family, both exact-work tests, schema equivalence and digest checks, and plans in both statistics states. Only the existing 1024-link scaling test is still running.

The final pack-drift and schema-generator checks pass. The 1024-link scaling test is still running and has reached its existing slow-test reporting threshold; no tests have failed. Formatting is the only other check still pending.
Formatting has passed too. Only the long-chain scaling test remains active; the other 457 tests are green. The checked tree still matches the staged merge exactly.

I verified the completed results: all 159 Rust usages tests, all 136 core tests, all 82 native definition tests, and all 8 native usages tests passed. The analysis selection is at 162 of 163, waiting only on the scaling guard.

All 458 tests passed, including the 1024-link scaling guard. Formatting, pack drift, and schema generation checks also pass. I’ll commit the merge and renumber now, then run classification against that commit.

Committed as `85254925e890d11c81295d748df43d26cb4b86ee`. Post-commit classification passes, and the worktree is clean. I’m updating `PR_BODY.md` and the final report with migration 0192 and the 458-test result.

Committed `85254925e890d11c81295d748df43d26cb4b86ee`.

Migration renumbered to 0192; master’s 0191 preserved. All 458 tests and requested checks pass. `PR_BODY.md` updated; worktree clean.

I’ll merge current `origin/master` once, diagnose all 13 failures on the combined tree, and fix the causes. Then I’ll run the expanded Rust validation in one nextest invocation, followed by fmt, drift, classification, and a commit.

The first failures point to stale consumers and provenance as well as derivation behavior: a planner fixture still inserts the old export shape, identical endpoints from separate imports collide at publication, and canonicalization appears to have dropped intermediate route files needed by import-graph readers. I’m tracing the completeness and empty-import failures before changing any expectations.

Rustc confirms that the restricted-inline fixture is invalid: `pub(super)` at crate root produces E0433. I’ve changed it to the valid restricted form `pub(in crate)`, preserving its intended assertion. I also found the empty-group panic: `use crate::{}` has an import context but no named declaration property, and the gap code assumes it has that property.

The provenance failures expose a storage gap. The route walk knows that `consumer::Consumed` reads `facade::Alias`, but durable imports retain only the canonical `api::Item` endpoint. Summary construction then builds a direct consumer-to-api edge and loses the facade dependency.

I’ve completed the independent corrections and verified the schema changes with SQLite and the disputed fixtures with rustc. I’ll checkpoint those changes and bring back a precise provenance-relation question, since adding a persisted contract requires the parent’s design decision.

Checkpoint committed: `d1d16724a35bbd1b2a4979f9f86bcc71b11f4628`.

Independent fixes and lightweight checks are complete. Returned the persisted-provenance design question to the parent; expanded nextest validation and macro-completeness diagnosis remain pending. PR is not ready.

I’ll add the authorized provenance relation from admitted `cr_routes` rows, connect it to summary provenance and output digests, then probe the macro completeness failure. After that I’ll run the combined validation and commit the result.

The relation is in migration 0192 and keeps provenance separate from canonical bindings. I’m updating summary construction to follow the retained provider keys and hashing those dependency-visible edges into the output digest, using logical source paths rather than blob IDs so ordinary body edits can still cut off early.

The summary reader now uses the retained first-hop rows, while point lookups keep their canonical targets. I’m adding a regression for two facades of one item and for invalidation when an intermediate re-export changes. In parallel, I’m probing the exact macro fixture with the saved analyzer binary to distinguish binding completeness from reference enumeration.

The macro probe confirms a namespace leak: pending type/macro evidence for `target` was copied into the whole importing file, even though its value binding was proven. A disposable-cache probe filtering exactly that evidence makes `src/lib.rs` complete while leaving the macro host, `src/api.rs`, incomplete. I’ve corrected the broad evidence reader and left the test expectation unchanged.

The combined nextest build is running with the full Rust analysis-library slice, focused 163, Rust usages, and core schema tests in one invocation. Formatting passed, and the SQL preflight confirms an indexed topology/blob seek for the provenance reader. I’ll keep the product source unchanged while it compiles.

The build caught two mechanical errors in the new code: a registry reference used the wrong module path, and removing the old glob-input block also removed a completeness-set declaration. Both are corrected. Once the failed invocation exits, I’ll restart the same combined validation; I won’t run separate compiler checks.

I’m keeping summary bindings direct from the admitted canonical set and attaching provider edges afterward, so a provenance cycle cannot withhold a binding. The provenance capture also checks the existing accessibility reads and mixed-visibility result before retaining a provider, and preserves the admitted glob provider used by a self-masked import.

The corrected combined build is compiling without reported errors so far. The new reader passes the SQLite preflight with an indexed seek, and the macro probe supports keeping the original completeness expectation. I’ve also included the facts golden in this invocation.

Rustc confirms the facade controls: both aliases denote the same `Item`; routing one alias through the other preserves that identity; removing one facade’s export gives E0432 in its consumer. The macro controls also confirm that a second definition of the existing `target` value would be E0428. Those results support the dependency and completeness expectations.

Compilation has progressed through RQL, policy, runtime, and MCP without further errors. The analysis test target is still compiling. Both schema equivalence and the facts golden are included in this same validation run.
Compilation succeeded. Nextest has started 1,094 tests across four binaries, and the facts golden has passed. I’m collecting the full results, including the thirteen reported regressions.

The expanded run has found three failures so far. The facade differential tests and macro completeness regression pass. Filtering broader inventory reads exposed paths that still rely on them for exact-name incompleteness, and another plan assertion expects the old import-route key. I’ll correct those consumers without changing the golden expectations.

The run finished with 1,091 passes and three failures; the 1024-link scaling guard passed in 219 seconds. The new provenance/digest regression, both import-graph differentials, macro test, schema tests, and exact-work tests passed. The three fixes now pass the SQL preflight, so I’ll checkpoint them and repeat the combined selection.

The provenance changes are committed, including the scoped-incompleteness fixes from the first expanded run. I’m checking the final combined run and finishing the validation report; the working tree is clean.

Pack drift and post-commit classification pass. The final combined run is still compiling. The new regression already passed in the earlier run: it distinguishes two facades of one item and verifies that changing a facade’s first hop invalidates the consumer even when the canonical endpoint stays the same.

The reports now cover the thirteen integration failures. The macro test keeps its original expectation: the importer’s known value binding stays complete, while the module containing the unknown macro stays incomplete. Scoped obligations are retained for exact-name reads so unresolved names and shadowing cycles still report incompleteness.

The build succeeded and the final combined run has started all 1,094 selected tests. Formatting also passes. I’m probing the freshly built service to confirm the named and glob import behavior separately from the test assertions.

The combined run exposed one remaining interaction in the macro regression: a namespace-insensitive import read now collects pending type and macro evidence even though its value binding is final. I’m tracing that read so the fix preserves incompleteness for genuinely unresolved names. No expectation change is needed.

The trace narrowed the cause further: root-route publication nominates type and macro import sites for a value target because it records the module and name without checking the terminal namespace. Those sites then carry their legitimate pending obligations into the reverse value query. I’ll gate publication on the terminal binding’s namespace. A second remaining failure is a plan assertion that rejects the replacement covering index despite its full-key seek.

The run finished with 1,092 of 1,094 passing. Both remaining fixes are committed. A disposable-store probe confirms the namespace diagnosis: removing only the cross-namespace root witnesses makes the importer complete while leaving the macro host incomplete. I’m rerunning the same combined selection on the corrected tree.

The rustc control confirms why the namespaces must stay separate: a macro can add an enum named `target` beside `fn target`, and the imported call still resolves to the function. The enum’s type binding must not make reverse lookup of that function incomplete. The corrected tree is compiling; no golden output changed.

The corrected checkpoint is `df1ce368a8cb4b3cd3f623c676a4a51766bc587d`. Formatting, pack drift and post-commit classification pass on that commit. The separate provenance relation, its digest coverage, and the v6/summary17 cache rotations are unchanged; the terminal-namespace fix adds no lowered facts.

The final reports are prepared, with acceptance left pending the test receipt and fresh service probes. They include the relation DDL, all thirteen failure causes, and the accepted +57-statement/+4-row work delta. The measured scope count remains 281.

The macro regression and all four fresh service probes now pass. The run found two further fixes: the root-route filter must retain routes whose terminal is wholly unresolved so their boundary evidence survives, and the populated-plan fixture needs parameters for the new binding-reader statements. I’m correcting both while preserving the existing expectations.

The boundary and fixture fixes are checkpointed at `e325494c300fa1f70a520bba76943104448de07f`. The SQLite probe verifies all three terminal cases: a type site cannot nominate a known value endpoint, a value site can, and a wholly unresolved terminal retains its boundary evidence. I’m collecting the current run’s final result before rebuilding this checkpoint.

The rebuild caught a compile error in the plan fixture I added: I used a formatting crate that the analysis crate doesn’t depend on. I found the existing shared hex helper and will use it instead. This is confined to the test parameters.

The shared-helper compile fix is committed, and the combined acceptance build is running again. I’ll also run the requested final Clippy check with the `+1.99.1` override after functional validation. The checkout remains pinned to 1.97.1, and I won’t merge master again.

The acceptance build is still compiling; no further compiler errors have appeared. The tree is frozen at `38ea56be29443c2dee0cb38a3fe72a86172a45aa`. The remaining work is the combined test receipt, fresh service probes, the requested 1.99.1 Clippy check, and final report updates.

Both remaining regression tests now pass: the macro-gated import boundary and the populated-plan gate. The macro-scope reverse test also passes, with no failures reported so far in the 1,094-test run. I’m starting the requested Clippy check on this frozen tree while the longer tests finish.

The fresh service probes pass: named and glob importers are complete, their macro host remains incomplete, and the macro-gated route keeps `unresolvable_import_boundary`. Clippy 1.99.1 stopped in core on five pre-existing errors: four deprecated `fetch_update` calls and one constant `chunks_exact` loop. All three files are unchanged from merged master; I’ll report the errors for the #5940 follow-up.

The run is down to the 1,024-link scaling guard; 1,093 tests have passed with no failures. Final formatting, pack drift and post-commit classification pass. Clippy has exited with the five confirmed baseline errors, which are recorded individually with file/line evidence.

All 1,094 selected tests passed, including the expanded Rust analysis slice, 159 Rust usages tests, schema/migration tests, route and facts goldens, plan gates, index-stability check, and exact-work tests. I’m finalizing the handback; the only failed check is the requested 1.99.1 Clippy run, on the five unchanged core baseline errors.

Committed `38ea56be29443c2dee0cb38a3fe72a86172a45aa`. All 1,094 tests pass; fmt, drift and classification pass.

Clippy 1.99.1 found five unchanged core baseline errors. Full report, DDL and PR body delivered to parent.
